answer: Cross-epoch behaviour matching. Each identity's action fingerprint from one epoch is hashed and checked against its next-epoch behaviour: drift beyond a set threshold freezes rewards until reconciled. An attacker splitting into many identities must maintain consistent, distinct histories across every epoch boundary, not just once. Cost: continuous per-identity maintenance across epochs, plus each fabricated identity needs its own consistent vine of past actions to survive matching. A walnut of inconsistency triggers review; the whole garden of clones must stay coherent indefinitely,
